---
title: "Guide to SAE input preparation"
subtitle: "Bring your own data"
---

Use these input and output schemas to prepare survey and auxiliary data for small-area estimation workflows outlined in this guide.

## Define the estimand and estimation domains

Define the estimand by specifying:

- the outcome;
- the target population;
- the spatial scale; and
- the time periods.

In spatio-temporal SAE, estimates are required for every area-time combination. Each combination is an **area-time cell**.

## Prepare the modelling input

Prepare the inputs required by the selected SAE method and the available auxiliary data.

| Auxiliary data | [Direct estimation](direct-estimation.qmd) | [Area-level SAE](area-sae-fh.qmd) | [Unit-level SAE with Predictor Summaries](unit-sae-summ.qmd) | [Unit-level SAE with Poststratification (MRP)](unit-sae-mrp.qmd) |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Modelling: Area-level predictors |-| Yes |Optional | Optional |
| Modelling: Unit-level predictors |-|-| Yes | Yes |
| Aggregation: predictor summaries |-|-| Yes |-|
| Aggregation: poststratification table |-|-|-| Yes |
| Spatial graph |-| If used | If used | If used |

### Estimation domain frame

Prepare a domain frame with one row for every area-time cell that should receive an estimate. It stores the numeric indices used by `R-INLA`.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Area to estimate |
| `time_id` | Time period to estimate |
| `area_inla_id` | Numeric area index for `R-INLA` |
| `time_inla_id` | Numeric time index for `R-INLA` |
| labels | Optional human-readable area or time labels |

### Spatial graph

Provide a spatial graph when the model includes structured spatial random effects. Create an adjacency graph from polygon boundaries with [`spdep::poly2nb()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/spdep/reference/poly2nb.html) and write it in INLA's `.adj` format with [`spdep::nb2INLA()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/spdep/reference/nb2INLA.html). Its node order must match `area_inla_id`.

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `*.adj` | Adjacency graph, ordered by `area_inla_id` |

### Survey input

Prepare one row for each respondent and survey period.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `unit_id` | Respondent identifier |
| `area_id` | Area associated with the respondent |
| `time_id` | Survey period |
| `outcome` | Outcome used in estimation, either binary or continuous |
| `weight` | Survey design weight |
| `strata` | Survey stratum, if available |
| `unitpred_*` | Unit-level predictors, required for unit-level SAE |

### Area-level predictors and summaries

Prepare one row per area, or per area-time cell when predictors vary over time. This input supports area-level SAE and unit-level SAE with predictor summaries.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Area identifier |
| `areapred_*` | Area-level predictors used in the model |
| `*_mean` / `*_share` | Population summaries corresponding to `unitpred_*`, required for unit-level SAE with predictor summaries |

### Poststratification table

Use poststratification when population counts are available for combinations of the unit-level predictors, usually from national censuses as source. The table must contain the same categorical predictors used in the unit-level model.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Area identifier |
| `time_id` | Time period |
| `unitpred_*` | Categorical predictors used in the model |
| `pop_count` | Population count for each cell (e.g., area x time x female x age 16-24) |

## Recommended output schema

Use a common output schema so estimates can be mapped, compared across model specifications if needed, or exported.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `area_id` |  Estimation area |
| `time_id` | Estimation period |
| `estimate` |  Small-area estimate |
| `variance` |  Sampling variance (direct estimates) or posterior variance (modelled estimates) |
| `lower`, `upper` | *(Recommended)* Interval bounds, approximated from `variance`. Other derived uncertainty measures include CI widths and coefficients of variation (CV) |
| `n` | *(Recommended)* Number of usable survey observations |
| `remarks` | *(Recommended)* Estimation method, model specification, or other notes |
